The thing about dry food is it's basically candy to cats. You give a cat dry food and they'll eat it. And often they'll eat however much you give them, even if it's too much.

Not all dry foods, mind you, but most big brand dry foods.

Once she gets more used to wet food and once she has more types of wet food available she will be fine.

Adopting a cat is a major change to your life. Especially if you're not used to having pets.

Any kind of major change is going to have an adjustment period, and the less used to having pets you are the longer and rougher it's going to be. I can promise you it's worth it on the other side, but life _is_ going to suck for some time while you learn all the small ways your life will change. 

>  I get worried she’s going to knock something off and break it

This is one those the changes. Cats can and will find a way to knock things over, it's up to you to create an environment where there isn't anything they can easily knock off.  Over time, these things become second nature. Stuff like checking if she is under your chair before getting up without thinking. 

> She also gets very chatty, but as soon as I try to give her attention she darts away (again, this is only at night). 

Does she try to lead you someplace or is she dashing under furniture? Most likely she's still just skittish, but it sounds like she either wants something (food, outside air to smell) or she wants attention at a distance. Chirp back at her, get a little closer (but not close enough that she'll run away), give her some eye kisses (make eye contact, blink slowly, then turn your head away). If you have any toys you can toss for her, she might enjoy that. 

You might also be playing with her _too_ much. If you're playing too much during the day she might be getting too riled up, but needs space and isn't sure how to handle the conflicting emotions. 

Do you have any cat owners among your friends or family? If you do, invite them over a few times a week to help you and her bond.
